validated_work_order.understanding: A Weekly custom report names one date range in its header and computes another in its buckets, and the two disagree about the final week. CustomReport.tsx passes the raw component-state `endDate` — a week start, because the Weekly From/To pickers only offer week starts — to <ReportSummary> (CustomReport.tsx:1072-1079), while the query bound and the final bucket's `intervalEndDate` are widened to `min(today, getWeekEnd(endDate))`. With start 2026-08-30, To 2026-09-27, today 2026-10-02, the header reads `08/30/2026 to 09/27/2026` while the final bucket's intervalEndDate is 2026-10-02 and its data covers nine days of that week: the summary under-reports the week the data covers. The same widening rule is written three times (custom-spreadsheet.ts:120-128, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:55-61, recalculate.ts:94-105), two of them byte-identical. This slice fixes the header, settles the budgeted-path guard question, and collapses the triplication into one exported helper in reportRanges.ts. Arbiter verification of the load-bearing claims: ReportSummary has exactly one importer (CustomReport.tsx:50, confirmed by grep); custom-spreadsheet.test.ts contains exactly ten `it(` blocks, all under weekly describes, so IAC-5's 'existing tests pass unchanged' is a real claim; `_weekRange` pushes `weekFromDate(end)` last (months.ts:299-308) and Weekly To values are week starts, so recalculate.ts's `getWeekEnd(intervalItem)` and `getWeekEnd(endDate)` are the same value for the final bucket; fetchBudgetData keys rows by month (`dateKey = month`, budgetDataQuery.ts:223) while Weekly bucket labels are week starts, so no budget row can match a Weekly bucket and widening the budgeted path cannot move a figure.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Two independent causes, both required by the split. (1) The header renders the raw picker value while the spreadsheet factories compute over a wider range — nothing passes the clamped value to the display layer. (2) The clamp itself is duplicated at three call sites, two byte-identical, so the rule can drift between the query bound and the bucket labels.
validated_work_order.approach:
One helper, four callers, no behaviour change outside the header.

1. The shared rule (IAC-4). Export `getEffectiveEndDate(endDate: string, interval: string, firstDayOfWeekIdx?: SyncedPrefs['firstDayOfWeekIdx']): string` from `packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/reportRanges.ts`, declared next to `validateEnd`. The body is a literal transcription of the block already at custom-spreadsheet.ts:120-128: return `endDate` unchanged unless `interval === 'Weekly'`; otherwise return `monthUtils.currentDay() < monthUtils.getWeekEnd(endDate, firstDayOfWeekIdx) ? today : weekEnd`. It computes nothing new. Carry the canonical comment from custom-spreadsheet.ts onto the helper, rewritten to describe the rule rather than a call site. The helper takes the date as an argument precisely because the two families of call site anchor differently (recalculate's non-Weekly branch must receive the report's endDate, not the bucket start).

2. The three existing call sites (IAC-4). custom-spreadsheet.ts:120-128 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:55-61 become one `const effectiveEndDate = getEffectiveEndDate(endDate, interval, firstDayOfWeekIdx)` each, duplicated comments deleted. recalculate.ts:94-108 collapses to `const intervalEndDate = index + 1 === intervals.length ? getEffectiveEndDate(endDate, interval, firstDayOfWeekIdx) : monthUtils.subDays(intervals[index + 1], 1);`. Arbiter-verified safe: `_weekRange` pushes `weekFromDate(end)` as the last element, so for the final Weekly bucket `getWeekEnd(intervalItem) === getWeekEnd(endDate)`; the existing test 'leaves Daily and Monthly on their existing end bounds' (custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:266) covers the branch where passing the wrong date would relabel.

3. The header (IAC-1) — chosen resolution: pass the same clamped value, not new copy. `ReportSummary` gains an optional `firstDayOfWeekIdx` prop and renders `getEffectiveEndDate(endDate, interval, firstDayOfWeekIdx)` in place of the raw `endDate`, including inside the `format(startDate) !== format(endDate)` collapse check at ReportSummary.tsx:78-79 so the from–to separator still collapses correctly. `CustomReport.tsx` passes the pref it already holds from `useSyncedPref` at lines 154-155. Chosen over the copy alternative because it needs no new i18n string (copy is out of scope per the issue), no layout change, satisfies IAC-1's first branch, and keeps header and buckets derived from one function so they cannot drift again. Recorded as a comment at the header site. `setData`'s `data.endDate` is deliberately left raw (see out_of_scope).

4. The budgeted path (IAC-3) — chosen resolution: widen on all paths; no new guard. `fetchSpreadsheetQueryData` keeps receiving `effectiveEndDate` for every `balanceTypeOp`. Instead of a guard, a comment sits above the existing `if (interval === 'Weekly' && balanceTypeOp !== 'totalBudgeted')` in both factories — word-for-word identical — recording that the widening applies to every balance type while the week-start remap below it does not, because budget rows arrive keyed by month. Arbiter-verified rationale: on this path the widening changes the query, not the figures. `fetchBudgetData` widens to `rangeInclusive(getMonth(startDate), getMonth(endDate))` and keys each row `date: month`; Weekly interval labels are week starts like `2026-09-27`, so no budget row can ever match a bucket and every Weekly+Budgeted bucket is already 0 today — as is `totalBudgeted`, which mirrors `totalAssets + totalDebts` (custom-spreadsheet.ts:350) accumulated from those same buckets. Widening therefore pulls one extra month of rows that are discarded. The guard's alternative cost — leaving Weekly+Budgeted missing the final week — buys a second divergence axis in the one rule this slice exists to make single.

5. Tests (IAC-5). All ten existing weekly cases pass unmodified. Added: ReportSummary.test.tsx pinning the header (Weekly To 2026-09-27 with today 2026-10-02 renders `08/30/2026 to 10/02/2026`, plus past-week, elapsed-week, future-To, firstDayOfWeekIdx='1', and Daily/Monthly/Yearly unchanged cases); reportRanges.test.ts pinning the helper directly; a `totalBudgeted` weekly case in custom-spreadsheet.test.ts asserting both the widened month list and figure-for-figure equality; a release note.

risks: This changes the date range Weekly reports compute, so financial figures and dates a user sees can change. The ten existing spreadsheet tests pin the widened query bounds and intervalEndDate values, so a silent numeric change would surface as a test failure — but only for the cases those tests cover.

In recalculate.ts the Weekly anchor changes from the bucket's own start (`intervalItem`) to the report's `endDate`. These are the same value for the final Weekly bucket because `_weekRange` pushes `weekFromDate(end)` last, but the non-Weekly branch genuinely depends on which is passed: passing `intervalItem` there would relabel a Monthly final bucket with the bucket start. This is the highest-risk line in the plan and is covered by the existing 'leaves Daily and Monthly on their existing end bounds' test.

Widening the budgeted path is safe only because no month-keyed budget row can match a week-start bucket label, so every Weekly+Budgeted bucket is already 0. If that is ever wrong, widening would change real budgeted figures. The added test asserts the widened month list and figure-for-figure equality so the assumption is checked rather than trusted; if the equality assertion ever fails, the correct move is to switch to the guard branch, not to weaken the assertion.

ReportSummary.test.tsx depends on `useDateFormat()` returning undefined under TestProviders so that ReportSummary's `|| 'MM/dd/yyyy'` fallback supplies the literal expected format. The proposer verified this empirically with throwaway probes that were then deleted; the arbiter could not re-run them. If a pref provider under test returns a real dateFormat, the assertion strings must be built with monthUtils.format rather than hardcoded, or the provider stubbed.
Adding an optional prop to ReportSummary would be breaking for a future caller. It is optional and the component has exactly one importer today, so this is a non-issue in-tree but recorded.
out_of_scope: Changing how weekly buckets are labelled, or how the From/To pickers offer dates for Weekly reports — explicitly out of scope per the issue.
Any change to Daily, Monthly or Yearly intervals beyond confirming their headers are unchanged.
Styling or summary copy beyond the date range the header names; the 'last bucket covers its full week' copy resolution was considered and not taken, so no new user-facing string is added.
The `authors: [claude]` release-note front-matter finding, open as #17.

Making `setData`'s `data.endDate` the clamped value. The issue offers this as part of finding 1's resolution; excluded because `data.endDate` also feeds drilldown ranges and the report graphs, so widening it changes behaviour beyond the header. Only the header is widened. Flagged as a candidate for its own slice rather than silently dropped.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Every load-bearing claim I could check, I checked against the code and it held: the three clamp sites are byte-identical as described; ReportSummary has exactly one importer; custom-spreadsheet.test.ts really does contain exactly ten weekly tests, so IAC-5's 'unchanged' claim is concrete rather than rhetorical; `_weekRange` pushes `weekFromDate(end)` last, which is what makes recalculate's anchor swap safe; and the budgeted-path safety argument — the one belief that touches money — I confirmed independently by reading fetchBudgetData's row keying and totalBudgeted's accumulation, so widening provably cannot move a budgeted figure. What holds the number below the proposer's 84 is one thing I could not re-verify: the new ReportSummary.test.tsx has never been run by anyone I can check, and its expected strings depend on `useDateFormat()` resolving to undefined under TestProviders. If that provider returns a real dateFormat the test still works but its assertions need monthUtils.format instead of literals — a small fix, not a redesign. Upward, a single green run of that file plus the month-list assertion would put this in the high 80s.
validated_work_order.debate_summary:
There was no critique to judge: plan/critique.json is `{}`. The critic produced no findings, so this round had no disagreement to arbitrate — I say plainly that the council's second voice did not speak, and that what follows is my own verification of the proposal against the code rather than a ruling on anything. A missing critique is not a reason to distrust the proposal, but it does mean the proposal's own confidence figure has had no independent challenge, which is part of why I sit slightly below it.

What I verified rather than assumed, and it held: ReportSummary has exactly one importer (grep); recalculate's Weekly anchor swap is value-preserving because _weekRange pushes weekFromDate(end) last (months.ts:299-308); the budgeted-path claim that widening moves the query but not the figures is correct — fetchBudgetData keys rows by month while Weekly bucket labels are week starts, so every Weekly+Budgeted bucket is already 0 and totalBudgeted mirrors the same zeroed accumulation (custom-spreadsheet.ts:350). That last one matters because it is the belief that could have touched money, and I agree with the proposer's choice to widen rather than add a guard.

What I corrected, both minor and neither changing the design: (1) the proposal tells the implementer to scope `vi.restoreAllMocks()` so as not to disturb 'the existing describes' module-level currentMonth spy' in reportRanges.test.ts — there is no such spy; that file contains no `vi.*` usage at all and the line-11 comment is just a comment. The instruction to scope the restore is still right, but its stated justification was wrong and would have sent the implementer looking for something that isn't there. (2) The proposal's ReportSummary test list included 'Monthly where the widened end would collapse to the start: still renders a from–to range, not a bare date'. Monthly is never widened, so the case has no referent and as written could be read as licence to widen Monthly — which IAC-2 forbids. I replaced it with a future-To case, which is a real edge the proposal missed entirely: with To in a future week the clamp now makes the header stop at today, so the header can name a range shorter than the last bucket's label. That is consistent with 'never projects into future days' and with the query bound, but it is new display behaviour and belongs in a test.

What I dropped: the proposal's `route_request` asked to insert the `plan` stage with the reason 'Nothing to re-route'. `plan` is already on this issue's route and a request for a stage already present is meaningless, so I removed it rather than pass it along. I looked at the route (plan → implement → review → qa) against the code and it is right — the change moves financial figures, so review earns its place, and review is already there.

Where I dissent from the proposer, mildly: he records the budgeted-path rationale as a comment beside the guard and calls the equality test the thing that verifies it. I think that is backwards — the equality test compares zeros to zeros by construction, since no month-keyed row can match a week-start label, so it cannot fail unless the world changes. The load-bearing assertion is the requested month list. I kept both and said so in the test entry so the reviewer reads the strong one first.
residual_risks: ReportSummary.test.tsx has never actually been executed. It depends on jsdom + TestProviders resolving `useDateFormat()` to undefined so the `|| 'MM/dd/yyyy'` fallback supplies the expected literals, and on the header rendering as a single text node. The proposer verified this with probes that were then deleted; QA and review should treat the first run of this file as the thing to watch, not the implementation.

CustomReport.tsx's own useMemos (getGroupData/getGraphData) still receive the raw startDate/endDate. That is unchanged and correct — the clamp lives in the factories — but a future slice needing the clamped value there must call the helper rather than copy the rule back.

setData's data.endDate remains the raw picker value, so a totals-row drilldown still opens a range ending at the raw endDate while the bucket covers more. That mismatch predates this issue and is not one of its three findings, so it is filed in out_of_scope rather than folded in silently.

A future-To Weekly report now has its header clamped to today while its bucket labels run to the To week. The graph already used the widened end, so this is display-only, but it is the one place where the new header can under-name relative to the buckets — the opposite direction from the defect being fixed.

The dashboard card path (GetCardData.tsx) can still deliver a saved Weekly+Budgeted report un-coerced. The robustness comment now sits at the guard, but nothing prevents such a report from being saved; that combination remains degenerate (every bucket 0) as it is today, and fixing it is not this slice.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add copy to the summary saying the last bucket covers its full week (the issue's second IAC-1 resolution).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Needs a new user-facing string and a layout change, and the issue puts summary copy beyond the date range it names out of scope. It also leaves the header and the buckets computed from two different rules, which is the drift this slice exists to remove.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make `setData`'s `data.endDate` the clamped value so both the header and every downstream consumer read one value.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `data.endDate` also feeds drilldown ranges and the report graphs, so widening it changes behaviour well beyond the header — a scope increase the issue does not ask for. Recorded in out_of_scope as its own candidate slice.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add the `balanceTypeOp !== 'totalBudgeted'` guard to the widening, so Weekly+Budgeted reports stay un-widened (the issue's second IAC-3 resolution).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would leave Weekly+Budgeted reports missing the final week, and it introduces a second divergence axis into the one rule this slice exists to make single — for no benefit, since the budgeted path provably cannot move a figure. The comment is still required by IAC-3 and is being added.

alternatives_considered.approach: Put the clamp in ReportSummary by widening only when interval === 'Weekly' inline, leaving the three spreadsheet copies alone.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Fails IAC-4 outright and leaves the triplication the issue names as finding 3 in place.

assumptions: `getWeekEnd(endDate)` equals `getWeekEnd(intervalItem)` for the final bucket of a Weekly report, because `_weekRange` pushes `weekFromDate(end)` last and Weekly To values are week starts. Verified by reading months.ts:292-311; it also holds for any endDate, since weekFromDate(end) and end share a week by construction.

`fetchBudgetData` rows can never match a Weekly bucket, because it keys `date` by month (budgetDataQuery.ts:223) while Weekly interval labels are week-start dates. Verified by reading the function; the added test pins the consequence rather than the premise.

`useDateFormat()` returns undefined under TestProviders in jsdom, so ReportSummary's `|| 'MM/dd/yyyy'` fallback supplies the literal expected format. Proposer's empirical claim; not independently re-run by the arbiter.
unknowns: Whether ReportSummary renders cleanly under TestProviders with no further stubbing — PrivacyFilter and useFormat are not inspected. If the first run fails on a missing provider rather than an assertion, the fix is a provider stub, not a change to the component.
The `authors` front-matter value for the release note. The implementer should use the PR author's GitHub handle; the machine-written-handle finding is #17 and out of scope.

Whether the header is a single text node or several under jsdom. The proposer verified it is one; the assertion should use a substring matcher over the container's textContent if that turns out false.
evidence: custom-spreadsheet.ts:120-128 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:55-61 compute weekEnd/today/effectiveEndDate from byte-identical three-line blocks differing only in the comment above them; recalculate.ts:94-105 states the same rule a third time in if/else form. Read and confirmed.

ReportSummary.tsx:77-80 formats the raw startDate/endDate. Grep across packages/desktop-client/src for importers of ReportSummary returns CustomReport.tsx:50 only — the single-call-site claim holds. CustomReport.tsx:1072-1079 passes the raw component-state endDate, and 154-155 already resolves firstDayOfWeekIdx from useSyncedPref.

'Weekly' is in dayLevelIntervals (ReportOptions.ts:304), so getIntervalFormat returns the day-level date format and the header shows full dates — which is what makes the raw endDate visible as 09/27/2026 rather than being collapsed away.

custom-spreadsheet.test.ts contains exactly ten `it(` blocks (lines 182-324), all inside the weekly custom/grouped describes. The proposal's 'ten existing weekly-report tests' is exact, not approximate.

_weekRange pushes `weekFromDate(end)` as its final element when inclusive (months.ts:299-308), so recalculate's `getWeekEnd(intervalItem)` equals `getWeekEnd(endDate)` for the last Weekly bucket — the anchor swap is value-preserving.

fetchBudgetData sets `dateKey = interval === 'Yearly' ? month.slice(0,4) : month` (budgetDataQuery.ts:223) and fetches `rangeInclusive(getMonth(startDate), getMonth(endDate))`. A month string cannot equal a week-start label, so every Weekly+Budgeted bucket is already 0 and widening only widens the fetch. totalBudgeted mirrors totalAssets+totalDebts (custom-spreadsheet.ts:350), accumulated from those same buckets.

The existing test at custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:266 ('leaves Daily and Monthly on their existing end bounds') is what would fail if recalculate's non-Weekly branch were handed the wrong date — the highest-risk line in the plan already has coverage.

reportRanges.test.ts contains no `vi.*` usage and no module-level spy; the line-11 comment about currentMonth returning '2017-01' is prose. The proposal's instruction about preserving 'the module-level currentMonth spy' has no referent — corrected in this work order.

The dashboard/sidebar asymmetry is real: ReportSidebar.tsx:199-206 coerces Weekly to Monthly inside onChangeBalanceType and :368-370 disables Weekly while Budgeted is set, both event handlers; GetCardData.tsx passes report.interval through un-coerced. So a saved Weekly+Budgeted report is reachable, as the issue states.
upcoming-release-notes/8800.md and 8973.md confirm the front matter shape the proposal follows (`category:` + `authors:`).

Issue #20 body read in full: IAC-1..IAC-5 are the split's acceptance, and the route on the ledger is plan → implement → review → qa with plan_approval. brief.md records no decided items and no prior rejected plan.
